title: Partitioned Scheduling and Parallelism Assignment for Real-Time DNN Inference Tasks on Multi-TPU
problem: Real-time DNN inference tasks on multiple TPUs exhibit scheduling anomalies due to variable execution times at different parallelism levels. Traditional gang scheduling cannot guarantee deadline satisfaction.
motivation: Edge devices require real-time DNN inference with guaranteed latency for responsive AI applications.
method: The approach separates TPUs into isolated partitions, where all DNN inference tasks (neural network computations) in each partition must run at the same level of parallel processing. This prevents scheduling anomalies—timing unpredictability that occurs when the same task runs differently depending on how many processors it uses. Since tasks in a partition always behave the same way, standard scheduling methods developed for single-processor systems can now guarantee that all tasks meet their deadlines.
key_novelty: Isolating TPU partitions with uniform parallelism within each eliminates scheduling anomalies in multi-TPU neural network inference.
contributions: Strict partitioning strategy for real-time DNN inference on multi-TPU systems
Joint optimization of parallelism levels and task-to-partition assignment
Schedulability verification approach leveraging uniform parallelism within partitions
Demonstrated higher schedulability ratio than gang scheduling on Edge TPU benchmarks
